title: PlayRates
summary: A full-stack video game tracking website
longDescription:
PlayRates is a video game tracking, rating and reviewing website. This app was originally a passion project of mine, as someone who loves to track my hobbies and couldn't find one for video games that met my requirements. However, it has now transformed into a live application with a small but growing, active user base.
Currently the application allows for the general functionality you would expect from a site like this, such as logging games with details, giving them a rating, and writing reviews. Another feature I added was a community, that allows for users to speak in threads about games and other topics. My goal and plan is to continue adding a wide variety of unique features that other sites in this space do not share, to stand out and be the most intuitive and feature-rich video game tracking platform there is.
The mobile experience in the application was built not just to be responsive, but to feel like a native application. It is a Progressive Web App (PWA), which allows the website to live on a phone like a real app. It also provides several important features for a native mobile experience, such as a bottom bar for navigation, optimised modals and interfaces, and easy use of all interactive elements.
The application is built using React on the frontend, with a backend written in Express.js. I also used Supabase both for authentication and a PostgreSQL database. The app has a large test suite, with continuous integration, which prevents any failing pull requests from being merged into main and therefore deployed into the live application on Vercel.
One extremely useful tool that I built into this project is the local development environment, which boots up a local Supabase in Docker, with a significant amount of preset data. This allows me to interact with, update, and delete data in a safe environment, to test functionality, and prevent any live data from being altered. This also allows me to work on the application whilst offline, where access to live data wouldn't be possible.
My ideas for the future of the application are endless, and my next steps are to implement new features and continue to maintain the site, whilst trying to expand the user base. My end goal is to build a large, active community, of people that share my love for this hobby.

title: booth
longDescription:
booth is a full-stack ticketing system app I am building, using React/TypeScript (frontend) and Go (backend). This is a long-term project that I am developing alongside my full-stack web development role, to apply my new knowledge and improve my comfort with a large scale code-base.
The app will use AI-powered functionalities to create an internal system for task management and assignment, and cross-functional collaboration within an organisation. booth is targeted at teams with varying technical knowledge, to assist in translating non-technical requests into technical solutions.
The app uses Supabase PostgreSQL as a database, and docker to containerize the build. I also plan to self-host n8n for AI functionality to create easily manageable AI workflows, which can be interacted with through simple webhooks from the code.
This project will also provide me with further experience in multiple other languages and technologies, as I will build external integrations to interact with the primary app, such as Discord/Slack Bots in Python/Node.js.

title: Clothing Shop
longDescription:
Clothing Shop is a full-stack e-commerce website, written using React/TypeScript (Frontend) and Go (Backend). This was my first project using Go, where I experimented with the language, and different libraries within Go, such as Zap for logging. Although I opted to use local json files for data storage instead of a database, for easier development, I still created a fully functional backend for providing data to the frontend, with serverside filtering.
Also in this project, for the first time, I experimented with testing libraries and implementing unit testing using Vitest and Go's built-in testing library.
This project was a great learning experience for me, where I used a lot of new technologies for the first time. In my next project, I plan to built upon this new knowledge further, with the implementation of a proper database, and continued experimentation with the Go programming language to further my knowledge and try out even more libraries and technologies.
